clue.text: Dreamily perceived fault in Isaacson's hose

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Jacob saw in a dream a stairway reaching to heaven
Jacob was Isaac's son, and a run in a stocking is called a ladder

explanation.surface: A fault in some Mr Isaacson's stockings is noticed as in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isaacson' reads as a surname; split it as Isaac's son, which is Jacob. A ladder is a run in a stocking or hose.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings point to the biblical stairway Jacob dreamt of, and to a run in the stockings of Isaac's son.

parts.note: in the Bible the walls of this city fell down at the sound of Joshua's trumpets

explanation.surface: A town whose walls let noise through.
explanation.walkthrough: Soundproof looks like a building complaint; it means the walls could not survive a blast of trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Joshua tells how the city's walls collapsed when the priests blew their horns and the people shouted.

clue.text: Firm came to terms with British aircraft

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
met as in met a demand or satisfied it

explanation.surface: A company made a deal over an aircraft built in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The de Havilland Comet was the world's first jet airliner, built in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland jet airliner of the 1950s was named after the heavenly body.

parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's opera Patience a fleshly poet loses the milkmaid of the title to his rival

explanation.surface: A sensual versifier who got exasperated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost patience' looks like losing one's temper, but Patience is the heroine of Gilbert and Sullivan's opera, whom the poet Reginald fails to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Reginald, the fleshly poet of Patience, ends the opera without the girl he courts.

clue.text: Was inclined, say, to be' fast

indicators.note: say tells us the word for leaning is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: leant means was inclined or sloped

explanation.surface: Someone tended towards going without food.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech LEANT rhymes with 'bent', so it sounds like the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The forty days before Easter are a traditional season of fasting in the Christian year.

clue.text: A hell of a beauty-spot? That's the message

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and Dante's name for the city of hell
a patch was a small piece of silk worn on the face as a beauty spot

explanation.surface: A gorgeous view described as a wonderful report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beauty-spot' looks like a scenic place; it is the cosmetic patch once stuck on the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official report or message sent from one place to another.

clue.text: They have a hangover on the house

definitions.text: They have a hangover on the house

parts.words: They have a hangover on the house
parts.note: the edge of a roof that overhangs the walls of a building

explanation.surface: People drinking free and suffering for it the next day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the house' suggests free drinks and 'hangover' their result; here the overhang is the roof edge jutting from the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower edges of a roof project beyond the walls, overhanging them.

definitions.meaning: fighter aircraft ordered into the air at once are sent up in a hurry
a climb over rough ground that needs skill, science meaning expertise

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the RAF order for fighters to get airborne fast, and a clamber over rocks using the hands.

indicators.note: out signals the letters of spider are put out of their order

explanation.surface: A spider was driven out of its hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SPIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To lever something open is to force it with a tool.

clue.text: They chew things over, indicating spirit in workers

parts.note: rum is a spirit
taken as written
ants are the standard crossword workers

explanation.surface: Something that ponders matters shows there is liquor among the labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They chew things over' looks like people deliberating; it means animals chewing the cud. 'indicating' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle, sheep and goats chew the cud, bringing food back up to chew again.

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A six-car train service from the Yorkshire town of Wakefield.
explanation.walkthrough: The man from Wakefield is the title clergyman of Oliver Goldsmith's novel The Vicar of Wakefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldsmith's novel is about a parish clergyman of the village of Wakefield.

parts.note: a memorable tune is one that hooks you; for anglers the word would mean good for hooking fish

explanation.surface: A song that would suit people out fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune that is easy to remember is said to be one that grabs the listener, just as anglers want to grab fish.

definitions.meaning: light ripples on calm water from a slight wind are given this name
in the fable the monkey uses a cat's foot to pull roasting chestnuts from the fire, so the name means dupes used by others

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a light breeze rippling water and people used as tools, from the fable of the monkey and the cat.

indicators.note: tangled up or intertwined, so the letters of rose and is are woven into a new order

explanation.surface: Roses are being woven into a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' rearranges ROSE and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Willow rods of this kind are the material woven into baskets, so the basketwork stands for them.

indicators.note: becoming tells us rattier and I turn into something new, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone growing crosser admits being annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' rearranges RATTIER with I.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy someone is to vex them.

definitions.meaning: a called-off event is said to be axed or dropped
to clean by rubbing hard with water

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both called off and cleaned thoroughly with water and a brush.

definitions.meaning: to emphasise
the equator is called the Line, and south of it is below it

explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise words you draw a line beneath them; south of the equator, called the Line, is beneath it.

parts.note: Edward Lear's nonsense poems include a nonsense adjective for a spoon and for a hat

explanation.surface: A hat of the sort worn by King Lear.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear is not Shakespeare's king but Edward Lear, the nonsense poet whose Owl and Pussy-cat dine with a runcible spoon and whose Quangle Wangle wears a runcible hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear invented the adjective and put it to both a spoon and a hat.

definitions.meaning: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England, so the place is gorge-like
splendid means magnificent or beautiful

explanation.surface: Someone praising a cheese with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar looks like the cheese; it is the Somerset village with its famous ravine, so the adjective splits as gorge plus -ous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word reads as 'having a gorge', like Cheddar, and normally means beautiful or magnificent.

clue.text: Make a monkey out of the historian

definitions.meaning: a long-armed ape of south-east Asia, loosely a monkey
Edward ... wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a long-armed ape and the eighteenth-century writer of The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.

definitions.meaning: to allude or turn attention to something
a notice paid for in a newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to allude to something, and the noun is a short form of advertisement, a notice in the papers.

clue.text: To type, getting money; is of current interest

parts.note: taken as written
pica is a size of printing type
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A typist who gets paid is newsworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical matters relate to present-day events and concerns.

parts.note: in The Tempest the spirit sings that after summer he flies merrily riding on a flying mammal

explanation.surface: How a sprite gets about in the fall.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel's song in Shakespeare's The Tempest runs 'On the bat's back I do fly after summer merrily'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song names a night-flying creature's back as the spirit's ride once summer has gone.

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman dismissed then heading off to bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbers game is played for money in halls, a form of betting.

definitions.meaning: to arise or occur unexpectedly
a harvest that goes up

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to occur unexpectedly, and read literally a harvest that rises.

clue.text: Plus four at dinner? How tasty!

definitions.text: Plus four at dinner? How tasty!

parts.words: Plus four at dinner? How tasty!
parts.note: add the word four and you have the small sweet cakes served with coffee at the end of a dinner

explanation.surface: A golfer's knickerbockers turning up at a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plus four' suggests golfing trousers, plus fours; it means this word plus 'four' gives petits fours, small cakes after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: French for small, it joins four to name the dainty cakes eaten after dinner.

indicators.note: in a down clue an ascent reads the pieces from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: A strategy for climbing a northern peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ascent' turns N and ALP upwards, giving PLA N.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or programme of action.

definitions.meaning: decimal means based on the number ten
happening many times

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word reads 'of ten', which is what decimal means; whole, it means many times.

indicators.note: the word in tells us fifty and is go inside the sea's name

parts.note: taken as written
L is fifty in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fifty missiles are in the northern European sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projectile' looks like a noun, a missile; here it is the adjective describing the flight of things fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the flight of things thrown or fired, so it works as the adjective 'projectile'.

clue.text: To. control the intellectual! describes the state's business

parts.note: to govern is to control
mental means relating to the intellect

explanation.surface: Ruling the clever people is what a state does.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is used for matters of the state and its administration.
